harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication on RHEL 9 across the cluster: node1 as writable primary, node2 and node3 as read-only async streaming standbys built via pg_basebackup with a dedicated SCRAM-authenticated replicator role. Verified writes on the primary propagate to both standbys and that standbys correctly reject writes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol (node2, node3, node1) with boot-id proof of restart and post-restart proof of PostgreSQL/replication recovery on each node, finishing with an end-to-end write-and-propagate check across all three nodes.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 13.23 on node1, node2, node3 and populated /etc/hosts with cluster names
Opened firewalld postgresql service (port 5432) on all three nodes
Initialized primary DB on node1; set listen_addresses='*', wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on, password_encryption=[REDACTED]
Added pg_hba.conf rules on node1 granting scram-sha-256 replication and general access from the 10.100.82.0/24 subnet
Generated a random replication password on node1 and created the replicator LOGIN REPLICATION role with a SCRAM verifier
Started PostgreSQL on node1, created repl_test table with a baseline row
Ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 on node2 and node3 to clone the primary and auto-generate standby.signal + primary_conninfo
Started and enabled PostgreSQL on node2/node3, confirmed pg_is_in_recovery()=true and streaming state in pg_stat_replication
Verified standbys reject INSERTs (read-only) and that INSERTs on the primary propagate to both standbys
Deleted the temporary password file from node1
Captured boot_id baseline on all three nodes, then restarted node2, node3, and node1 sequentially via systemctl reboot, polling each until command execution and boot_id change confirmed restart
Enabled the postgresql service on node2/node3 (previously start-only) so it survives reboot; verified auto-start after restart on all nodes

After each restart verified PostgreSQL active, correct recovery state, and full repl_test data present; after final node1 restart performed an end-to-end insert-and-propagate check confirming replication to both standbys

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as writable primary with replication enabled
evidence.summary: Primary initialized, wal_level/max_wal_senders/hot_standby set, pg_hba.conf configured for replication access, service started, replicator role created

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only streaming standbys
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R successfully cloned primary onto both nodes creating standby.signal and primary_conninfo; both started as active with recovery mode enabled
pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both 10.100.82.11 and 10.100.82.12 in state=streaming
INSERT on node2 fails with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'

evidence.requirement: changes committed on primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 confirmed present on both node2 and node3 via SELECT
Captured boot_id b634b53f... and confirmed postgresql active before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and boot identity change
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, node unreachable during restart, then boot_id changed to 1982e0cf... confirming restart
postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=false (primary), data intact, both standbys reconnected streaming, new insert propagated to both standbys
Captured boot_id f1afbc7f... and confirmed postgresql active before restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and boot identity change
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, node unreachable, then boot_id changed to cc56cecd... confirming restart
postgresql started (had to be manually started/enabled after first boot since it was previously start-only), pg_is_in_recovery=true, full repl_test data present, primary confirms streaming resumed
Captured boot_id 98aa35f5... and confirmed postgresql active before restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement and boot identity change
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, node unreachable, then boot_id changed to 656cbfe7... confirming restart
postgresql active automatically (enabled prior to reboot), pg_is_in_recovery=true, full repl_test data present including rows inserted while node2 was mid-restart
Diagnosed and fixed password_encryption mismatch (md5 stored hash vs scram-sha-256 hba requirement) that was blocking replicator authentication
